fix #50842 

fix code: 

```js
import { it, before, describe, after } from 'node:test';

describe('failing test suite', () => {
  before(async () => {
    console.log('before called');
    throw new Error('error');
  });

  after(async () => {
    console.log('after called');
  });

  it('should be ok', async () => {});
});
```

issue_context.title: After inside describe is not executed when the before has an error
comments: Hey @MoLow, please confirm this issue, if it's a bug I would love to open PR for this.
I would expect this to be the behavior, dont think it is a bug
I'm a bit confused if this would be intended behaviour when in the global scope it behaves differently? @MoLow

review_comments: You don't need the console log here, the must call is enough

yes, but that shows unexpected behavior. :/
the tests pass for both common.mustCall() and common.mustNotCall() cb in after hook if we didn't pass any fn inside mustCall and mustNotCall. 
That's why I used console.log to test the actual expected behavior.

Are you saying that the following code won't work?
```js
after(common.mustCall(() => {}));
```
yes, test pass with this change and also with `after(common.mustNotCall(() => {}));` (which is totally unexpected) :/
